title: Outliers & skewness
examples: How far from the box is an outlier?
What does it mean if the box plot is skewed?
Can you show me an example of a skewed dataset?

explain.say: Today we learn about outliers and skewness in data. An outlier is a data point far from others. We use the box plot to spot these points easily.

items: Outlier: data point far from others
Use box plot to spot outliers

explain.say: First we look at the interquartile range or IQR. The IQR is the middle half of your data values. It is calculated by subtracting the first quartile from the third quartile.

To find an outlier we use the one point five times IQR rule. We calculate the lower fence by subtracting one point five times the IQR from the first quartile. The upper fence is the third quartile minus one point five times the IQR.
A data point outside these two fences is an outlier. For example if the lower fence is ten and a point is five it is an outlier. We also look at the box plot shape to see skewness.

items: Outlier: < Lower Fence OR > Upper Fence
Check box plot shape for skewness

faq.q: What is the interquartile range exactly?
faq.a: The interquartile range is the spread of the middle fifty percent of your data. It tells us how spread out the central values are.
asks: How do I find the middle half spread?

faq.q: How do I use the one point five times IQR rule?
faq.a: You find the lower fence by subtracting one point five times the IQR from the first quartile. You do the same for the upper fence using the third quartile.
asks: Can you explain the 1.5 times IQR rule?

faq.q: What does it mean if my box plot is skewed?
faq.a: Skewness means the data is not symmetrical around the middle. If the tail is longer on one side it is skewed in that direction.
asks: What does a skewed box look like?

faq.q: Are outliers always bad for data analysis?
faq.a: Outliers can sometimes be errors, but sometimes they are real extreme values. You must check if they are valid data points first.

faq.q: Does the box plot show the mean?
faq.a: No the box plot shows the median which is the middle value. The mean is a different measure of central tendency.
asks: Where is the average on a box plot?
Does the box plot show the mean value?

facts: The median is the middle value in an ordered dataset.
The box plot shows the quartiles: Q1, median, and Q3.
Outliers are points significantly distant from other data points.
A perfectly symmetrical dataset will have a balanced box plot.

quiz.say: A dataset has Q1 of twenty and Q3 of sixty. The IQR is forty. The lower fence is:
quiz.why: The lower fence is found by subtracting one point five times the IQR from the first quartile.

wrong.0: This adds the two quartiles together which is incorrect for finding a fence.
wrong.1: This only subtracts the IQR from the third quartile, ignoring the lower fence rule.
wrong.2: This only subtracts the full IQR instead of one point five times the IQR.

quiz.say: If a box plot has a long tail pointing to the right, the data is:
quiz.why: A long tail to the right indicates that larger values are pulling the data in that direction, which is positive skewness.

wrong.0: While often related, 'normally distributed' is a specific curve shape, not just describing the tail direction.
wrong.2: Negative skewness has its long tail pointing to the left side of the plot.
wrong.3: Symmetrical data would have tails that look balanced on both sides.

quiz.say: Which measure is most affected by extreme outliers?
quiz.show: Which measure is affected by outliers?
quiz.why: The mean uses every single value in its calculation, so extreme outliers pull the mean towards them.

wrong.1: The median only cares about the middle position and ignores how far the ends are.
wrong.2: The range uses the absolute minimum and maximum, which are highly affected by outliers.
wrong.3: The IQR is based on quartiles, which are more resistant to extreme values than the mean.
